mapping_basis: All 13 source photo hashes match the readiness record. Caption labels #1–#9 are mapped to canonical stanzas 1–9; photos 005 and 006 both carry #5 and are both mapped to stanza 5. Stanza 10 has no photo or caption and is planned from canonical Sanskrit only. Photo/caption mismatches are recorded per stanza; canonical Sanskrit controls the scene. Photos 011–013 are text screenshots, not scene references.
source_photo_role: Captain-supplied scene context only; not style or identity references, not approval.

references.caption: #1 The magnanimous Bali was killed by Lord Indra. Bali came back to life & grew in power because of Sukracharya’s 'vishwajit' sacrifice and conquered three worlds. Devas hid themselves in the fear of being killed by Bali
references.observed_reference: The reference is a two-panel composite: Bali enthroned at left and Shukracharya beside a serpent at right. It supports Bali’s revival and conquest context but includes no Indra or hidden Devas.
references.mapping_note: Use only for Bali/Shukra identity and story context; compose the canonical victory and Deva fear as one matte mural scene.

references.caption: #2 Aditi, mother of Devas, seeing the sad plight of her sons, requested Kashyapa, her husband to help. He asked her to do payovrata worship for twelve days to Bhagwan.
references.observed_reference: Aditi sits with joined hands before seated Kashyapa in a riverside forest; it aligns with her appeal and the payovrata instruction.
references.mapping_note: Follow the canonical twelve-day payovrata action; source image is provisional scene context, not rendering or identity approval.

references.caption: #3 Aditi completed the worship in twelve days with sincerity and devotion. Bhagwan appeared before her with four arms and said that Bhagwan himself will be born as a son to them, but to keep it a secret.
references.observed_reference: A four-armed blue deity appears before a kneeling woman in an ornate dark setting; it aligns with the divine promise to Aditi.
references.mapping_note: Use the mapped divine appearance and Aditi context; recompose matte and retain exactly four attached divine arms.

references.caption: #4 On the auspicious day of Dwadashi and Thrivonam Nakshatram together, Bhagwan was born to Goddess Aditi with Chaturbhujam, sanku chakra, gadha, padmam.
references.observed_reference: A vertical devotional image shows a luminous four-armed deity and a woman with an infant; it suggests the birth but adds a cosmic display not specified in the stanza.
references.mapping_note: Depict the canonical birth to Aditi on the auspicious day; do not copy the added cosmic staging.

references.caption: #5 The Devas in great joy were showering flowers on Bhagwan and were blowing trumpets. Goddess Aditi & Kashyapa were praising Bhagwan with folded hands & just then Bhagwan took on the form of a talented handsome Brahmach
references.observed_reference: A letterboxed children’s animation frame shows Aditi holding a newborn. It depicts the birth, not stanza 5’s celebration and Vamana’s transformation.
references.mapping_note: Photo/caption label #5 does not match the depicted birth action; follow stanza 5, not the newborn image.

references.caption: #5 The Devas in great joy were showering flowers on Bhagwan and were blowing trumpets. Goddess Aditi & Kashyapa were praising Bhagwan with folded hands & just then Bhagwan took on the form of a talented handsome Brahmach
references.observed_reference: A letterboxed children’s animation frame shows a youthful Vamana among figures in a celestial setting, fitting the transition from divine birth to the brahmachari form more closely than photo 005.
references.mapping_note: Use as scene context only; remove all embedded writing, logo, bars, digital rendering and unsupported staging.

references.caption: #6 Father Kashyapa performed upanyanam to Bhagwan and offered sacred thread, stick, deer skin, and a garland of beads. Bhagwan performed the rites with the sacred fire and departed for the house of Bali where the Ashvame
references.observed_reference: A devotional painting shows Bali seated while Vamana’s feet are washed by a woman with a water vessel; it is a later Bali welcome scene, not the initiation or departure in stanza 6.
references.mapping_note: Photo/caption label #6 mismatches its depicted Bali foot-washing scene; follow the canonical upanayana and departure.

references.caption: #7 Vaamana held the umbrella as though he wanted to mask the might of the asuras and carried stick as if to punish the asuras. Bhagwan’s body weight shook the earth.
references.observed_reference: A small Vamana with umbrella and staff walks across a pale background; it supports stanza 7’s journeying brahmachari and props.
references.mapping_note: Use only for story/prop context; recompose as a full-bleed landscape and exclude its pale blank field.

references.caption: #8 As Vamana approached the banks of Narmada, his radiance blindfolded Shukrachaarya and other sages and they wondered who he could be?, is he the Sun or Agni or Sage Sanatkumara?!.
references.observed_reference: A cosmic Trivikrama image shows one giant four-armed form spanning the earth and sky with a small Vamana below; it does not depict the approach to the Narmada or sages shielding their eyes.
references.mapping_note: Photo/caption label #8 mismatches the cosmic stride; follow canonical stanza 8 with Vamana arriving at the Narmada sacrifice and Shukra/sages unable to see clearly.

references.caption: #9 All the sages welcomed Vamana in to the yagnakootam. Mahabali seeing the young Brahmin in full radiance, was happy to receive him and washed his feet with holy waters and sprinkled that water on his head. knowing that
references.observed_reference: Bali receives a youthful Vamana under a canopy while attendants gather; it broadly aligns with the welcome in stanza 9, though the foot-washing is not clearly shown.
references.mapping_note: Use for Bali’s courtly welcome only; depict the canonical washing of Vamana’s feet and Bali receiving the water on his head.
